message:
fix(update): the acknowledgement could stop existing before the updater opened it

The host set the ack event and closed its handle immediately. The updater
did not open that event until it needed the answer, at PrepareForSwap. If
the host's was the last handle, the named object went with it -- so an
acknowledgement that really was delivered could not be found, the updater
stood down, and the host was already on its way out because it had agreed
to leave.

Every return value in that sequence was correct. What went missing was a
handle, which is why a test over the bool seams would not have caught it;
the regression works on the real named handle's lifetime instead. It has
the fix, a counter-example that opens late and finds nothing while the
host still returns ExitNow, and the case where there is no channel at all.

So the updater opens the channel before it signals and holds it until the
answer arrives. If it cannot open it, it does not signal -- telling
someone to leave when you have no way to hear their reply is the same
mistake in the other direction. And the host no longer returns ExitNow
when SetEvent fails or there is nothing to set: agreeing to go is only
safe once the agreement has been delivered.

Separately, the deadline was computed as GetTickCount() + timeout in 32
bits, which wraps on a machine that has been up 49.7 days -- and then
every wait ends at once claiming the updater ran out of time. It is a
64-bit subtraction now, in its own function with an injectable clock, so
the boundary can be tested rather than reasoned about. WAIT_FAILED ends
the wait explicitly instead of spinning on the same failure until the
deadline and then blaming the timeout.

And the measured "328ms to notice a death" is narrowed where it was
written down. It does not cover a death before the mutex is taken, and it
follows the thread that holds the mutex rather than the process -- the two
coincide because the working copy takes it on its main thread and holds it
to exit. That is a contract, not a property of the operating system, and
it now says so.
